es: Escribir una queja exagerada y una respuesta bromista con so/such… that, un correlativo y suavizadores que mantengan el buen tono.

teaching.en: Hyperbole is exaggeration on purpose: “I have been waiting for a hundred years” turns a short delay into a joke.
teaching.es: La hipérbole es exageración a propósito: «Llevo esperando cien años» convierte una demora corta en una broma.
teaching.explanationEs: Nadie lo toma al pie de la letra: por eso hace reír en vez de mentir.
segments: Hyperbole is exaggeration on purpose: “I have been waiting for
a hundred years” turns a short delay into a joke.
teaching.audioText: Hyperbole is exaggeration on purpose: “I have been waiting for a hundred years” turns a short delay into a joke.

teaching.en: When friends exaggerate a mock complaint, such as “This coffee is so weak that it is practically water”, everybody understands the game.
teaching.es: Cuando los amigos exageran una queja en broma, como «Este café es tan flojo que casi es agua», todos entienden el juego.
teaching.explanationEs: So + adjetivo + that + resultado absurdo: la estructura típica de la queja exagerada.
segments: When friends exaggerate a mock complaint, such as “This coffee is
so weak that it is practically water”, everybody understands the game.
teaching.audioText: When friends exaggerate a mock complaint, such as “This coffee is so weak that it is practically water”, everybody understands the game.

teaching.en: A softener such as kind of or only joking keeps an exaggeration friendly, because it shows that no harm is meant.
teaching.es: Un suavizador como kind of o only joking mantiene amistosa una exageración, porque muestra que no se quiere hacer daño.
teaching.explanationEs: Los suavizadores avisan del tono: sin ellos, una broma puede sonar a ataque.
segments: A softener such as kind of or only joking keeps an
exaggeration friendly, because it shows that no harm is meant.
teaching.audioText: A softener such as kind of or only joking keeps an exaggeration friendly, because it shows that no harm is meant.

teaching.en: Both the complaint and the reply are exaggerated, yet both writers stay polite and take the edge off the moment.
teaching.es: Tanto la queja como la respuesta son exageradas, pero ambos autores siguen siendo corteses y quitan filo al momento.
teaching.explanationEs: Both… and une dos elementos; el verbo va en plural.
segments: Both the complaint and the reply are exaggerated, yet both
writers stay polite and take the edge off the moment.
teaching.audioText: Both the complaint and the reply are exaggerated, yet both writers stay polite and take the edge off the moment.

teaching.en: Either a joke makes everyone smile, or it can go too far; neither result is pure luck.
teaching.es: O una broma hace sonreír a todos, o puede pasarse de la raya; ninguno de los dos resultados es pura suerte.
teaching.explanationEs: Either… or ofrece dos opciones; neither… nor las descarta, con el verbo en afirmativo.
segments: Either a joke makes everyone smile, or it can
go too far; neither result is pure luck.
teaching.audioText: Either a joke makes everyone smile, or it can go too far; neither result is pure luck.

teaching.en: Hyperbole such as “the worst day in history” is out of proportion to a late bus, and that gap makes it funny.
teaching.es: Una hipérbole como «el peor día de la historia» es desproporcionada para un autobús que llega tarde, y ese desfase la hace graciosa.
teaching.explanationEs: Out of proportion: la distancia entre lo dicho y lo ocurrido es el motor de la broma.
segments: Hyperbole such as “the worst day in history” is out of
proportion to a late bus, and that gap makes it funny.
teaching.audioText: Hyperbole such as “the worst day in history” is out of proportion to a late bus, and that gap makes it funny.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje de Tom: ¿cuál es la hipérbole?

choices.text: honestly, it was kind of a disaster
but I am only joking about the whole thing
so long that I could have written a novel

feedback.es: La hipérbole es el resultado absurdo con so… that; kind of y only joking son los suavizadores que rebajan el tono.

hint.es: Busca la parte que nadie podría creer al pie de la letra.

origin.text: Tom sent his friend a message after the concert: “The queue was so long that I could have written a novel. Honestly, it was kind of a disaster, but I am only joking.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Ni mi hermano ni mi hermana probaron un trozo.»

feedback.es: Neither se completa siempre con nor, nunca con or: los dos elementos quedan descartados.

hint.es: Es la pareja negativa de neither.

origin.text: The pizza was so small that I could have eaten it in one bite, and neither my brother ___ my sister got a single slice.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Fue una cola tan larga que aprendí italiano.»

answer.text: It was such a long queue that I learned Italian

feedback.es: Such a + adjetivo + nombre va seguido de that + resultado absurdo: la hipérbole queda completa.

hint.es: Such a va antes del adjetivo y del nombre; that introduce el resultado.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje: ¿qué hace la hablante con «the driver is on holiday»?

choices.text: She exaggerates to be funny and then softens the remark.
She reports a rumour that she has heard from other passengers.
She makes a serious accusation and then regrets it at once.

feedback.es: Nadie cree que el conductor esté de vacaciones: es una hipérbole cómica que «only joking» suaviza inmediatamente.

origin.audio: I have been standing at this bus stop for so long that the birds know me by name. The timetable promises a bus every ten minutes, but I am almost certain that the driver is on holiday. Only joking, of course. I am sure that he will arrive soon, and I will forgive him at once.

prompt.es: Lee la respuesta a Tom: ¿por qué podría resultar ofensiva?

choices.text: It mocks Tom's own effort, and the softener comes too late.
It exaggerates so much that nobody could possibly believe a single word.
It contains no softener at all, so it sounds sincere.
It praises the pasta in a way that sounds false.

feedback.es: La broma apunta al esfuerzo del anfitrión y el suavizador final llega después del golpe: no consigue quitar el filo.

origin.text: Dear Tom, your pasta was so heavy that the table needed a rest, and you clearly believe that cooking is either an art or a test for your guests. No offence, of course.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tanto mi teléfono como mi paraguas dejaron de funcionar.»

answer.text: Both my phone and my umbrella stopped working

feedback.es: Both… and une los dos sujetos y el verbo queda en plural: stopped working.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario radiofónico: ¿por qué funciona la exageración de la columnista?

choices.text: It hides her real opinion of the train behind jokes she does not mean.
It expresses genuine tiredness without turning the complaint bitter.
It shows that commuters on her train really do swap birthdays.
It follows a rule from her editor that every column must contain a joke.

feedback.es: La exageración expresa un cansancio real sin volver amarga la queja: los chistes la suavizan y la regla del editor limita el daño.

origin.audio: In her column about public transport, the writer complains that her morning train is so crowded that she has learned to sleep standing up, that the train is such a tiny space that commuters exchange birthdays by the third stop, and that neither the conductor nor the timetable has ever told the truth. Readers love it, because nobody believes a word of it. The exaggeration is her way of saying that she is tired, and the jokes soften a complaint that might otherwise sound bitter. Her editor adds only one rule: never go too far, and never aim the joke at a person who could be hurt.

prompt.es: ¿Qué busca con la broma del comienzo quien responde a Sara?

choices.text: To turn the complaint into a joke so that it can be forgotten quickly.
To share the blame with the kitchen staff in a friendly way.
To keep the mood friendly while still taking the complaint seriously.
To avoid offering a solution by making the whole matter a joke.

feedback.es: La broma exagera el problema para acercarse a Sara, y el almuerzo gratis y el cierre serio demuestran que la queja sí se toma en serio.

origin.text: Dear Sara, I am sorry that your sandwich was cold. It was such a dramatic disaster that I have asked the kitchen to hold a minute of silence. Only joking: I have already arranged a free lunch for you, and I hope that this small gesture shows how seriously we take every complaint.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una sonrisa y un «solo bromeaba» pueden quitar filo a una queja.»

feedback.es: Take the edge off es la expresión fija para suavizar algo que resultaba demasiado duro.

origin.text: A quick smile and an “only joking” can ___ the edge off a sharp complaint. Without them, even a friendly exaggeration might sound like an attack.

prompt.es: Escribe una queja exagerada y la respuesta bromista de un amigo (180–240 palabras).

answer.text: My complaint is simple: the queue at the post office was so long that I learned to play the guitar while I waited. It was such a slow morning that the clocks went on strike, and both my patience and my shoes were worn out before I reached the window. Either the post office has forgotten how to count, or the staff are training to become statues. I am kind of upset, but I am only joking. My friend Leo answered at once: Poor you! You are so dramatic that the theatre should call you. Neither the queue nor the clerk deserves such an unfair review, but either you take a book next time, or I will bring you a chair. Only joking: come to my house, and I will make you a hot chocolate.
accepted: My complaint is simple: the queue at the post office was so long that I learned to play the guitar while I waited. It was such a slow morning that the clocks went on strike, and both my patience and my shoes were worn out before I reached the window. Either the post office has forgotten how to count, or the staff are training to become statues. I am kind of upset, but I am only joking. My friend Leo answered at once: Poor you! You are so dramatic that the theatre should call you. Neither the queue nor the clerk deserves such an unfair review, but either you take a book next time, or I will bring you a chair. Only joking: come to my house, and I will make you a hot chocolate.

Here is my complaint about the bus. The journey was so slow that I finished a whole novel, and the seat was such a hard seat that I now walk like a robot. Both my phone and my umbrella stopped working, and neither the driver nor the weather said sorry. Either the bus company has lost the map, or the driver is taking the scenic route around the planet. I am sort of tired, but I am just joking. My friend Mia replied: Poor you! You are so brave that you deserve a medal. Either you leave earlier, or I will buy you a bicycle. Only kidding. Come for dinner tonight, and I will cook pasta, so we can complain about the bus together.

feedback.es: Una respuesta completa exagera con so… that y such a…, reparte la queja con un correlativo y mantiene el buen tono con un suavizador.

origin.text: Escribe en inglés una queja exagerada sobre algo cotidiano (una cola, un atasco, un autobús) y la respuesta bromista de un amigo. Usa dos estructuras de intensidad (so… that y such a…), un correlativo (both… and, either… or o neither… nor) y un suavizador (kind of, only joking).

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura defiende el autor del blog sobre la exageración?

choices.text: It is a form of lying that speakers should avoid.
It is acceptable in every situation, between any two people.
It is acceptable whenever the speaker says that he is only joking.
It is acceptable when both sides know that it is not literal.

feedback.es: Antes la veía como mentira; ahora la entiende como un pacto: es aceptable mientras ambos saben que no es literal y el tema no hiere.

origin.text: I used to think that exaggeration was a form of lying. Now I see that it is a kind of contract: the speaker promises not to be taken literally, and the listener promises to laugh. The contract breaks only when the joke is about something that the other person cannot change, because then nobody is playing a game any more.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ni el autobús ni el clima tuvieron la culpa.»

answer.text: Neither the bus nor the weather was to blame

feedback.es: Neither… nor concuerda con el sujeto más cercano (the weather) y el verbo va en afirmativo: was.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de mi hermano: ¿qué queja es real y no una exageración?

choices.text: The length of the film he watched.
The price of the ice cream he bought.
The low temperature inside the cinema.

feedback.es: El helado congelado y los créditos eternos son hipérboles; el «kind of serious» revela que lo que de verdad le molestó fue el frío.

origin.audio: My brother sent me a complaint about the cinema. He said that the room was so cold that the ice cream froze, and that the film was so long that the credits felt like a holiday. Then he added that he was kind of serious about the cold, because he had to borrow a stranger's coat. I replied that he should bring one next time.
